summary: This article explains why golf rewards careful, accurate shots instead of raw power, how scoring and clubs work, and why fewer strokes always wins.
introduce: Drop a pencil and ask, “What was the cause? What was the effect?” to model the idea quickly. Then show the title “Golf: Precision Over Distance” and tell students to look for things in the article that make other things happen.

keyTerms.def: one hit of the ball in golf
the long, mowed strip of grass between the start and the hole
the quality of being exact and correct

challengeTerms.def: the quality of being very exact and accurate
the ability to direct or manage something exactly as intended
a careful plan for reaching a goal

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that hitting the ball far matters more in golf than hitting it accurately? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Do you agree that accuracy matters more than distance in golf?
struggling: Pre-teach stroke, fairway, and accuracy with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses precision, control, and strategy to explain one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
